AI Tools & Licenses
This page provides an overview of common generative AI tools, a field that is constantly growing and changing. The use of Microsoft Copilot as well as Google Gemini and NotebookLM is currently recommended, as data-protected access is possible directly via an ETH account.
The scope of application of AI goes far beyond the tools listed here. The ETH AI Center is working intensively on

various application scenarios, including in the field of teaching, and is the central hub for artificial intelligence. Some possibilities of application in the field of teaching, which are currently being developed, are listed under projects . You can also find specific information on the direct use of these tools under Assistance for Teaching .
Apertus
(Image: EPFL, ETH Zurich, CSCS / Molinari Design)
The language model external page Apertus was developed in collaboration between ETH Zurich, EPFL, and CSCS (Swiss National Supercomputing Center). It serves as a foundation on which developers and organizations can build future applications, such as chatbots, translation systems, and digital l

earning tools.
The entire development process, including architecture, model weights, training data, and methods, is freely accessible and comprehensively documented. Initial impressions of the multilingual model can be gained via the test platform external page Try Apertus . Detailed information about the project can be found on the website of the external page Swiss AI Initiative .
Recommended generative AI tools
The page on AI-Tools at ETH Zurich provides an up-to-date overview of the growing landscape of various AI tools. The Gemini and NotebookLM offerings from Google, as well as Copilot from Microsoft, which are accessible via an ETH cloud subscription, are available to all ETH employe

es and students via secure access. It is therefore recommended that these tools be used primarily for teaching purposes.
Status, October 2025
The external page Microsoft Copilot Website (formerly Bing Chat) is a tool based on generative AI that can generate text and images and is available free of charge. The service can be accessed in a protected environment via a Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscription , which is provided by ETH Zürich.
In addition to direct web access, Copilot is also integrated directly into the Edge browser and can also be used via your ETH account. An overview of the entire product range (including M365 Copilot and Github Copilot) is available on the website Microsoft Copilot

from IT Services.
The freely accessible version of Microsoft Copilot offers
freely available text and image generation,
the ‘ protected ’ status (with Microsoft ETH-account ), whereby personal data is not used as training data,

Plagiarism check
Please note that access to the plagiarism detection software is exclusively intended for professors and lecturers of ETH Zurich. Students and employees without the lecturer role cannot use Turnitin Originality.
(Access to Turnitin Originality (with ETH account))
Turnitin Originality is a web-based text similarity detectio

n software. Submitted documents are compared against an extensive database of academic papers (both published and unpublished), books, journals, and other sources:
Some features:
Doc-to-doc comparison: direct comparison of a document with one or up to 5 other documents.
Detecting plagiarism: Turnitin Originality detects similarities in texts including paraphrasing, citations and references.
Originality reports: The tool generates an originality report that highlights all the areas of the document that match the sources in the database. The report also shows the percentage of similarity and the matching sources.
Checking quotations and references: Turnitin Originality can check citations and

references in submitted documents to ensure that they are properly formatted and incorporated correctly.
There are a few things to keep in mind when using Turnitin Originality:
Note the confidentiality level: Only documents classified as "public" or "internal" may be uploaded to Turnitin Originality for similarity checking. For more details, see the Download terms and conditions of use (PDF, 143 KB) .
Understand the limitations: Turnitin Originality is not infallible. It relies on its source database and may not detect all instances of plagiarism, for example, if the source is not in the database. Turnitin Originality is not a substitute for teaching proper citation and referencing practices

. Instructors should guide students on correct citation and referencing. Here, the ETH Library offers support.
Watch out for false positives: Turnitin Originality can mark text as plagiarised even if it is properly cited. It is important to carefully review the flagged text to determine if it is indeed plagiarised or a false positive.
False positives: Turnitin Originality may flag sections of texts as plagiarised even if they have been cited correctly. Always check highlighted sections carefully to determine if they have really been plagiarised or if the software has merely produced a false positive.
Use the software responsibly: Plagiarism detection software should be used in a responsible

and ethical manner. Selective use only in cases of suspicion prevents a culture of mistrust. The following use cases are possible: Plagiarism check of written work of students from the teaching context such as term papers and bachelor's/master's theses: The plagiarism check is carried out by supervisors (usually professors or lecturers) if plagiarism is suspected. If the suspicion is confirmed, it is communicated by the supervisors to the ETH's Office of Legal Affairs in Teaching and further processed together with them. Plagiarism check of written work that is produced in the context of a doctorate: Term papers, papers, abstracts, doctoral theses. The examination is carried out by superviso

rs (professors or lecturers) if plagiarism is suspected. If the suspicion is confirmed, it will be communicated by the supervisors to the ETH Research Ethics via trusted persons and followed up. Plagiarism check of texts produced in the context of research: Papers, abstracts, habilitation theses, etc. The check is carried out by members of the department (mostly professors or lecturers) if plagiarism is suspected. If the suspicion is confirmed: proceed as described in the previous point.

This page is only available in English.
Safe use of AI Before exploring the capabilities of these tools, follow our Information Security Guidelines to ensure compliance with ETH Zurich’s data protection and security standards. Review the official recommendations here . Users are responsible for using AI tools in an authorized and responsible manner. See Guide for Users of AI at ETH Zurich . Uploading strictly confidential data to external cloud services, including AI tools, is prohibited. The work mode of M365 Copilot without the web search option is approved for use with confidential

data . The web search option is disabled in the work mode by default. M365 Copilot Chat and the web mode of M365 Copilot is approved for internal data . AI tools lacking a cloud assessment have not been released for use with ETH data. Processing confidential, strictly confidential, or protected personal data is not permitted. AI‑generated output must be reviewed before use.
Data classification Information owners classify the information according to the risk-oriented approach as explained in RSETHZ 203.28 Appendix 1a Information is classified as “ strictly confidential ” if unauthorised access could damage the interests of ETH Zurich. It must not be stored on external cloud services and may

only be shared with a specifically authorised group under strict security precautions. Information is classified as “ confidential ” if unauthorised access could significantly damage the interests of ETH Zurich. It must be limited to specific authorised individuals and securely stored. Information is classified as “ internal ” if unauthorised access could damage the interests of ETH Zurich. Such information is therefore generally intended solely for members of ETH Zurich. Unless explicitly stated otherwise, all data and information at ETH is considered “internal”. Information is considered public if it is authorized for publication by the responsible body.
